Subject: Horizon EHR -> Redwood: BAA and subprocessor questions for upcoming integration

Hi Tessa,

Appreciate the intro from Procurement — we at Horizon are evaluating Redwood as the inference layer for a clinical summarization workflow that will touch PHI. Before we schedule a demo, procurement asked us to confirm a few things from your side so we can scope legal and technical review on our end: 

- Do you execute a HIPAA BAA that covers inference workloads by default, or is that an addendum? If an addendum, can you provide a draft we can review?
- Can you provide a current subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessors process PHI (and if so, which ones)?
- We need to understand where egressed or cached data may be stored — do you offer US-only residency for PHI?
- Any SOC 2 or FedRAMP docs we should expect?

I've attached a simple dataflow diagram (Horizon_Dataflow_v2.png) that shows the high-level integration. Our procurement window is tight — target decision by the end of August.

If you can send a short note on feasibility and any relevant documents, I can route to our legal/security and procurement teams.

Thanks,

Thanks Tessa / Sarah — adding some legal context and an initial artifact.

1) BAA: Redwood executes a BAA for customers processing PHI. I've attached a redline-friendly Word doc (BAA_Redlines_Tessa_Marcus.docx) with our standard clauses; the usual negotiation points are: permitted processing, subprocessors, data deletion/return, audit rights, and liability caps. For most EHR integrations we accept limited carve-outs (e.g., standard-of-care exceptions) but we're flexible on indemnities for heavier custom work.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor list. Most subprocessors do not access plaintext PHI; inference compute (GPU) is typically ephemeral and managed by our cloud provider. For PHI workloads we offer Dedicated and Private deployment options to isolate processing and storage. If you prefer, we can provide a list explicitly indicating which subprocessors may be in the path for a given hosting option.

3) Data elements: please confirm whether the payload to Redwood will include direct identifiers (MRN, SSN) or if Horizon will pseudonymize before calling our API. The presence of persistent identifiers affects retention and audit requirements.

4) Timeline: I can turn around a redline response within 3 business days once we get Horizon's redline back.

Attachments: BAA_Redlines_Tessa_Marcus.docx

--

Hi Sarah — quick security/ops notes based on the diagram attached.

- Hosted API path: by default, our hosted model endpoints process tokens in ephemeral compute in the region you select. We perform automatic prefix/KV caching for performance — for PHI we recommend either Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or our Private (VPC) deployment to avoid cross-tenant caching.
- Residency: we can commit to US-only residency for both compute and persistent caches/logs if Horizon requires that in the contract. That will drive an implementation decision (Dedicated in a US region vs Private with customer VPC).
- Subprocessors: our infra stack includes cloud providers (AWS), monitoring, and model-ops partners. We can provide a redacted list today and a full list under NDA if needed. Note: some managed kernel/acceleration vendors may be involved depending on the GPU profile.
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II report available; we can provide SOC evidence and a short security questionnaire. For regulated clients we commonly do a 1–2 week security intake plus an architecture call.

Could you attach the dataflow with a slightly higher resolution (file size ok) and mark where PHI is created vs persisted vs ephemeral? That will help us scope the private vs dedicated recommendation.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
